Definition: a primary particle, denoting a supposition, wish, possibility or uncertainty:--(what-, where-, wither-, who-)soever. Usually unexpressed except by the subjunctive or potential mood. Also contracted for G1437.
BiblicalUsage: This little word never stands alone in English — it is the particle that turns a statement into a possibility: 'if', 'when', 'whoever', 'whatsoever'. Jesus says not one jot or tittle shall pass from the law till all be fulfilled, and whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do. It appears over a hundred and fifty times, quietly doing the work of 'if' and 'whatever' in the promises and warnings.
TheologicalSignificance: A particle carries no theology of its own; its weight is in the sentences it shapes — the conditions on God's promises and the certainty behind them.
